summary: FOUR OWNER CALLS ANSWERED WITH MEASUREMENTS TAKEN ON THIS TREE TODAY, AND TWO OF THE REFERRED ITEMS WERE ALREADY FIXED BEFORE I STARTED. Call 1's reporting-only option has LANDED (opt.restart.wraps / below_bar / no_reading, the report line and the gate reason that says 'DETECTED is what the rate ratio could see and not the number of restarts'), and so has the phantom-restart-on-resume repair (opt.ckpt.lr_prev_cleared); repair_sig's worry that the root discards the WarmupReport is also fixed -- compose() now binds it and warns on 'collapsing'. CALL 1: the blinding reproduces (at wavelength 210 over 2068 steps with damping OFF, 5 of 9 wraps detected at lr_decay=1.0 against 9 of 9 at lr_decay=0.0), and I found a THIRD blinding nobody has filed -- at lr_decay=1.0 the last wrap rises only 1.46x, so the >1.5x RATIO condition rejects it before the magnitude bar is consulted and no counter records that. The brief's 'compare against the cycle's own priced peak' option is REFUTED: a wrap is priced AT its own cycle's peak (measured 100.0% at all 15 wraps across four configurations), so that bar is not stricter, it is absent. RECOMMENDATION: split the one boolean -- drive the damping from the structural WRAP (complete by construction) and keep the magnitude test for StepOutcome.restart, the self-inflicted-shift stamp FAB reads, with the warmup suppressed by the `in_warmup` flag the function already holds instead of by `lr > 0.5*peak` (measured: the step-range guard suppresses exactly the one ramp false positive, at step 2, and nothing else). Everything except the counters is a TRAINING change and I priced it: mean rate over the run moves from 20.3% of peak to 16.6% at wavelength 300, 19.1% to 13.8% at 210, 20.1% to 15.8% at wavelength 6000 over 48,000 steps. It is INERT at the shipped defaults, which fit exactly one cycle at every run length I built (1000, 2068, 48000), so no recorded result moves. I recommend AGAINST changing OPT_LR_DECAY: it is gated on n>1 and therefore already inert at the shipped defaults, and turning it off leaves the damping ratchet blinding itself after two applications anyway (measured: 2 of 6 at lr_decay=0.0). CALL 2: the cost is 9.00 bytes per float exactly -- 433 kB per checkpoint at 48,000 steps, 2.52 MB at longrun.sh's 280,000, 18.9 MB of writes across a CKPT_EVERY=20000 run, 1.54 MB resident -- but the expensive part is the ESTIMATOR: the pooled whole-run p99 cannot answer Q-OPT-3's own question, which asks for the norm distribution AT the ~6000-step turn (measured, a pooled p99 of 8.53 hides a 7.9x per-segment swing). Reservoir sampling is disqualified twice (p99 error mean 15.5% worst 43.0% at k=1024, and it would need an RNG stream OPT does not have -- RNG_SUBSYSTEMS has no 'opt'); a ring buffer is off by -68% to -73% on p99 and is the exact defect state_dict already names. RECOMMENDATION: a fixed log-spaced histogram per run segment (24 x 200 bins = 4,848 ints, ~44 kB, constant in run length), which keeps the RANK exact, quantises only the VALUE (measured within 1.4% of exact p50 and p99 at 200 bins), is deterministic, composes across a resume by ADDITION, and must print its resolution or it becomes this project's characteristic failure. CALL 3: YES, a fourth verdict is needed, but the cut proposed in the brief is the wrong one -- 'no step ran' is not where the damage is. I drove all five arms that return 'budget' and two of them run the WHOLE budget and still cannot produce any verdict; one of those, at legal lever values, returns verdict='budget' on an encoder whose separation is 5.96e-08, and src/spine/compose.py branches only on 'collapsing', so the RUN-LEVEL FAILURE warning is not emitted. The right predicate is `collapse_points` being empty -- already computed in warm_up -- and the right fourth spelling is the spine's own UNREACHABLE state applied to a record. CALL 4: the shipped SIG_WARMUP=800 / SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=500 admit exactly ONE probe and ZERO stop points; a probe costs 0.16x of a warm-up step, so eight probes cost 0.16% of the budget. RECOMMENDATION: move SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY to 100 and leave SIG_WARMUP at 800, which is one lever, respects the file's own carry-forward hazard about changing two together, and is a TRAINING change (the stop can now fire early) that must be measured rather than assumed. Every recommendation names its falsifier and, where one exists, the GPU run that settles it.

findings.detail:
CALL 1 -- THE RESTART DETECTOR'S BLINDING. RECOMMENDATION: SPLIT THE ONE BOOLEAN INTO THE TWO THINGS IT IS ALREADY BEING ASKED TO BE. Drive the damping ratchet from the WRAP (st.cycle_index advanced, already computed and already counted as opt.restart.wraps), and keep the MAGNITUDE test for StepOutcome.restart -- the self-inflicted-shift stamp FAB is given -- but suppress the warmup false positives with the step-range flag the function already holds (`in_warmup`) instead of with `lr > 0.5 * peak`.

WHAT I READ. src/opt/api.py::maybe_step now reads, verbatim:
    peak = float(opt.lr)
    jumped = bool(st.lr_prev > 0 and lr > 1.5 * st.lr_prev)
    restart = bool(jumped and lr > 0.5 * peak)
and its own docstring justifies the second condition SOLELY as a warmup suppressor: 'the warmup ramp climbs from zero, so every early step multiplies the previous rate by far more than 1.5 and each one was logged as a "cosine restart" (observed at steps 15 and 31 of an 18-epoch run, at 2% and 3% of peak)'. The same boolean then gates BOTH `st.restart_amp *= float(opt.lr_restart_damp)` (clause 4, what the model sees) and the returned StepOutcome.restart, which src/spine/compose.py::LOOP_ORDER's OPT.maybe_step row names as 'one of the three self-inflicted shifts a capacity blackout would be OR-ed from' and whose comment block on shift_at_windows lists 'the E draw row's resample, the B TOK.mint_burst retok, and OPT's LR restart'. ONE NUMBER, TWO CONSUMERS WITH OPPOSITE REQUIREMENTS -- the growth controller wants 'did the rate actually jump enough to explain a loss jump', the ratchet wants 'did a cycle end without paying'. That is the root, and every option in the brief is a way of picking one consumer over the other.

RE-VERIFIED AGAINST THE CURRENT TREE BEFORE ANY ANALYSIS. Two of the three filed items are ALREADY FIXED and are reported separately: the reporting-only repair (opt.restart.wraps, opt.restart.below_bar, opt.restart.no_reading, the report line and the gate reason) has landed, and the phantom restart on a lengthening resume is closed by opt.ckpt.lr_prev_cleared. THE BLINDING ITSELF REPRODUCES. Driving the real build/scaled_backward/maybe_step/counters path over a 2068-window horizon at OPT_LR_WARMUP=20 with OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP=1.0 (damping off, so this is the CEILING on detection):
    wl=1200 decay=1.0 wraps=1 detected=1 | decay=0.0 detected=1
    wl= 700 decay=1.0 wraps=2 detected=1 | decay=0.0 detected=2
    wl= 520 decay=1.0 wraps=3 detected=2 | decay=0.0 detected=3
    wl= 400 decay=1.0 wraps=4 detected=2 | decay=0.0 detected=4
    wl= 300 decay=1.0 wraps=6 detected=3 | decay=0.0 detected=6
    wl= 210 decay=1.0 wraps=9 detected=5 | decay=0.0 detected=9

A THIRD BLINDING NOBODY HAS FILED, MEASURED HERE. At wl=210 decay=1.0 the counters read wraps=9, detected=5, below_bar=3 -- and 5+3 is 8, not 9. Pricing every wrap with src/opt/api.py::lr_at shows why: the last wrap (step 1864) rises only 1.46x (1.000e-04 -> 1.461e-04, 7.3% of peak), so the >1.5x RATIO CONDITION rejects it before the magnitude bar is ever consulted, and no counter anywhere records that. Removing the 0.5*peak bar entirely therefore does NOT recover every wrap: measured over the same series, a ratio-only detector sees 8 of 9 at wl=210 decay=1.0 and 6 of 6 at wl=300 decay=1.0. Only the STRUCTURAL wrap count is complete, which is the substance of the recommendation.

WHICH OPTIONS ARE REPORTING-ONLY AND WHICH CHANGE WHAT THE MODEL SEES -- the owner's whole concern.
  REPORTING-ONLY (and already shipped): the wraps/below_bar/no_reading counters, the 'opt.restart:' report line and the opt.lr.restarts gate reason that now says 'DETECTED is what the rate ratio could see and not the number of restarts'. Nothing about the rate moved.
  TRAINING: ANY change to the `restart` boolean, without exception, because that boolean is the only gate on `st.restart_amp *= opt.lr_restart_damp` and st.restart_amp is a multiplier inside src/opt/api.py::_schedule. Quantified, by replaying the schedule with each candidate detector, every cycle losing, at the shipped damp=0.5 -- the number is the MEAN RATE OVER THE RUN as a percentage of peak, i.e. literally what the model sees:
    wl=300 decay=1.0 (7 cycles, 6 wraps): shipped 20.3% | ratio-only 14.2% | step-range 16.6% | wrap-driven 16.6%  (detections 1 / 4 / 3 / 6; final restart_amp 0.5 / 0.0625 / 0.125 / 0.0156)
    wl=300 decay=0.0                    : shipped 24.0% | ratio-only 15.5% | step-range 18.8% | wrap-driven 18.8%  (detections 2 / 6 / 6 / 6)
    wl=210 decay=1.0 (10 cycles, 9 wraps): shipped 19.1% | ratio-only 11.9% | step-range 13.8% | wrap-driven 13.8%  (detections 1 / 4 / 4 / 9)
    wl=6000 decay=1.0 over 48,000 steps (8 cycles, 7 wraps): shipped 20.1% | ratio-only 13.6% | step-range 15.8% | wrap-driven 15.8%  (detections 1 / 4 / 4 / 7)
So the change is worth roughly an 18-28% relative reduction in the average rate on the multi-cycle arm, and nothing at all elsewhere -- see the next paragraph.

IT IS INERT AT THE SHIPPED DEFAULTS AND THAT BOUNDS THE RISK. Building at the shipped levers with run_windows of 1000, 2068 and 48000 gives n_cycles=1 every time (the OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=0 sentinel sets wavelength=run_steps and the warmup can never exceed a tenth of the run), so there are no wraps, the detector never fires, and src/opt/api.py::_schedule's envelope is gated on `n > 1` so OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0 is itself inert. EVERY RECORDED RESULT IS UNAFFECTED BY ANY OF THESE OPTIONS. The blinding is exclusively a property of the arm an operator reaches by setting OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH -- which is the arm the package's own docstring says goal A needs.

ALTERNATIVES, AND WHY EACH LOSES.
  (a) DO NOTHING YET -- keep the shipped detector, keep the reporting repair that has landed. This is the cheapest honest answer and it is not a strawman: nothing in a shipped run changes, the report no longer lets a reader take opt.restart.detected as a restart count, and the closed loop cannot fire at all today because best_bpb has no producer (src/spine/compose.py::LOOP_ORDER, OPT.maybe_step row: 'best_bpb HAS NO PRODUCER ... so opt.restart.damped and opt.restart.damp_refused_n1 are UNREACHABLE, not zero'). It loses only when the owner runs the multi-cycle arm WITH an EVAL Reading, at which point src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers' promise -- 'a schedule whose restarts keep failing anneals ITSELF off within two or three of them' -- is false at every lr_restart_damp <= 0.4737 and the ratchet judges 1 of 6 losing cycles.
  (b) COMPARE AGAINST THE CYCLE'S OWN PRICED PEAK. REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT -- filed separately against src/opt/api.py::_schedule. In one line: a wrap step is priced at p=0, i.e. AT its own cycle's peak, so `lr > 0.5 * cycle_peak` is `lr > 0.5*lr`, true at every wrap in every configuration I priced (own_cycle_peak = 100.0% at all 15 wraps measured). It is not a stricter bar, it is no bar, so it cannot do the warmup-suppression job the condition exists for.
  (c) DROP THE MAGNITUDE BAR (ratio-only). Reinstates exactly the false positive the docstring names. Measured on the current 1-based ramp (`lr * step / w`), a ratio-only detector fires ONCE per run, at step 2, because the ramp's ratio is k/(k-1) and only k=2 exceeds 1.5: at resolved warmups of 20 / 100 / 1000 that is 10.0% / 2.0% / 0.2% of peak. One false positive per run is not catastrophic, but it damps on a step where nothing wrapped and it stamps FAB with a self-inflicted shift at the start of every run.
  (d) SUPPRESS THE WARMUP BY STEP RANGE (`jumped and not in_warmup`). This is the brief's third option and it is the RIGHT REPLACEMENT for the magnitude bar, measured: the step>warmup guard admits none of the ramp's jumps at every warmup tested, i.e. it suppresses EXACTLY what the 0.5*peak bar was added to suppress and nothing else. It costs one identifier -- `in_warmup` is already unpacked from `_priced` three lines above the detector and is already used by the below_bar counter -- no lever, no wire, no state, no RNG. It loses ALONE only because it still inherits the ratio condition's own blind spot (8 of 9 wraps at wl=210 decay=1.0), which is why the recommendation pairs it with (e) rather than choosing between them.
  (e) DRIVE THE DAMPING FROM THE WRAP. Complete by construction (9 of 9, 6 of 6, 7 of 7 in every arm measured) and it is what src/opt/levers.py::OPTLevers already promises. Its cost is precise and must be stated: as the SOLE definition of `restart` it would also stamp FAB with a self-inflicted shift on wraps that barely move the rate -- the wl=210 decay=1.0 wrap at step 1864 raises the rate 1.46x to 7.3% of peak, which is not a plausible explanation for a loss jump. That is why the recommendation is a SPLIT and not a substitution.
  (f) FLOOR THE BAR ON restart_amp (bar = 0.5 * peak * (min_frac + (1-min_frac)*restart_amp)). Fixes the damping half of the blinding and not the envelope half: measured with restart_amp held at 1.0, where that correction is a no-op, the envelope alone still hides 3 of 6 wraps at wl=300 and 4 of 9 at wl=210. Folding the envelope multiplier in as well makes the bar equal the priced peak, i.e. it degenerates into (b).
  (g) CHANGE OPT_LR_DECAY -- filed separately, recommended AGAINST.

WHAT THE RECOMMENDATION COSTS AND FORECLOSES. It spends no wire (both values are already on the state or already returned; the 6 remaining wire edges are untouched), adds no lever, mints no RNG stream, and changes no signature: StepOutcome keeps its four fields and `restart` keeps its meaning for FAB. It DOES change what opt.restart.detected counts -- it would become the magnitude-detected count with a step-range warmup guard -- which is why opt.restart.wraps must stay printed beside it. It forecloses one thing: after the split, 'a restart' is no longer a single fact about a run, and any future reader wanting one number has to be told which. That is a cost I would pay, because the two consumers genuinely want different numbers and the project's characteristic failure is exactly one number standing for two.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, IN TWO STAGES, AND THE OWNER HAS THE GPU.
  STAGE 1 IS RUNNABLE TODAY WITH NO CODE CHANGE AT ALL and it settles whether any of this matters. Three arms over 48,000 optimizer steps at the shipped geometry, one seed set of >= 3 seeds: (A) OPT_LR_SCHED=none; (B) shipped single-cycle cosine (OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=0); (C) OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=6000 OPT_LR_WARMUP=1000, which fits 8 cycles. Read held-out bits/byte through the ~6000-step turn the package docstring is about, and read opt.restart.wraps against opt.restart.detected off OPT.counters (both now printed). FALSIFIER: if (C) does not beat (B) at and after the turn by more than the seed spread, warm restarts are not on goal A's path, the detector question collapses to a reporting question, and the answer is (a) do nothing -- close it.
  STAGE 2 ONLY IF (C) WINS, and it needs EVAL to produce a Reading carrying a seed count first (see unfinished). Same arm (C), same seeds, two detectors: shipped versus the split. FALSIFIER: if final held-out bits/byte differ by less than the seed spread, the detector change is cosmetic and the reporting-only answer stands. If the split arm is BETTER, the measured mean-rate table above is the mechanism and the lever finally does what it says. If the split arm is WORSE, that is the most interesting outcome available here -- it would mean the damping is harmful and OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP should default to 1.0 (off), which no amount of reading can establish.

findings.detail: THE BRIEF'S SECOND OPTION -- 'replace the relative bar with one that cannot be lowered by the mechanisms it feeds (compare against the CYCLE'S OWN priced peak rather than the run peak)' -- IS REFUTED BY THE SCHEDULE'S OWN ARITHMETIC, and I am reporting it as refuted rather than quietly not choosing it. src/opt/api.py::_schedule prices a step as cyc = min_frac + (1-min_frac) * 0.5 * (1 + cos(pi*p)) with p = ((step - w) / per_c) % 1.0. At a wrap, p wraps to ~0, so cos(pi*p) ~ 1 and cyc ~ 1.0 -- the wrap step IS the cycle's peak, whatever the damping and the envelope have done to it, because both multiply the whole cycle uniformly. So `lr > 0.5 * cycle_peak` evaluates to `lr > 0.5 * lr`, which is true for every positive rate. MEASURED: pricing every wrap in four configurations (wavelength 300 and 210, lr_decay 1.0 and 0.0, 15 wraps in total) the wrap rate is 100.0% of its own cycle's priced peak in EVERY case, against 95.3% / 82.1% / 63.0% / 41.9% / 22.9% / 9.7% of the RUN peak at wavelength 300 lr_decay 1.0. The proposed bar therefore has no discriminating power at all: it is not a stricter test than the run-peak bar, it is the absence of a test, and in particular it cannot suppress the warmup false positives (steps 15 and 31 at 2-3% of peak) that are the documented reason the second condition exists. It would degrade to ratio-only, which is option (c) in finding 1 and loses there on its own merits. WHAT THE OPTION WAS REACHING FOR IS REAL and is served instead by the step-range warmup guard plus the structural wrap count -- see finding 1.
findings.repro: .../own/opt_alt.py prints, per wrap, prev / lr / ratio / % of run peak / % of own-cycle peak, with the cycle peak taken as max over the priced rates carrying that cycle index. Column 'own_cycle_peak' reads 100.0% at all 15 wraps across wl in (300, 210) x lr_decay in (1.0, 0.0). Counterfactual counts in the same output: SHIPPED / ratio-only / ratio+steprange / ratio+own-cycle-bar = 3/6/6/6 at wl=300 decay=1.0 and 5/8/8/8 at wl=210 decay=1.0 -- the own-cycle-bar column is identical to ratio-only in every row, which is the refutation.

findings.detail:
CALL 1, FOURTH OPTION: DO NOT CHANGE THE SHIPPED OPT_LR_DECAY DEFAULT. RECOMMENDATION IS TO LEAVE IT AT 1.0. Three measured reasons, in order of weight.
  (1) IT IS INERT AT THE SHIPPED DEFAULTS, SO CHANGING IT BUYS NOTHING WHERE THE PROBLEM IS REPORTED. src/opt/api.py::_schedule gates the envelope on `enveloped = decay > 0.0 and n > 1 and run_end > w`, and building at the shipped levers gives n_cycles=1 at run_windows of 1000, 2068 and 48000 (the OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=0 sentinel makes one wavelength span the run). Measured. So today OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0 and OPT_LR_DECAY=0.0 produce bit-identical schedules on every shipped run, and the default is only a decision about the arm an operator opts into.
  (2) IT DOES NOT ACTUALLY FIX THE BLINDING. With the damping live at the shipped OPT_LR_RESTART_DAMP=0.5, replaying wavelength=300 over 2068 steps with every cycle losing gives detected=2 of 6 wraps at lr_decay=0.0, final restart_amp latched at 0.25 -- the ratchet still switches its own sensor off after two applications, because a damped wrap peaks at lr*(min_frac + (1-min_frac)*restart_amp) and clears 0.5*lr only while restart_amp > 0.4737. Turning the envelope off removes ONE of the two blinding mechanisms and leaves the one that is algebraic and configuration-free. A default change that half-fixes a defect is worse than none, because it makes the remaining half look like a different bug.
  (3) IT WOULD MOVE WHAT THE MODEL SEES FOR A REASON THAT IS ABOUT AN INSTRUMENT. Replaying wavelength=300 with the shipped detector, the mean rate over the run goes from 20.3% of peak at lr_decay=1.0 to 24.0% at lr_decay=0.0 -- the envelope is a real annealing mechanism, not a reporting artefact, and src/opt/api.py::_schedule's own comment records that the `n > 1` gate and the final floor clamp were added precisely so that lr_decay could be turned ON at all (it 'sat at 0.0 from the day it was written' because a single cycle ended at lr_min_frac SQUARED). Reverting the default would undo a repair, not a defect.

ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED. (a) Change the default to 0.0: loses on all three counts above. (b) Keep 1.0 but make the detector immune -- that is finding 1, and it is the change that actually answers the question the default was being asked to answer. (c) Do nothing at all, including finding 1: defensible today because the arm is opt-in and the report now says the instrument is partial; it loses the moment the owner runs the multi-cycle arm.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT, AND IT IS GPU WORK THE OWNER HAS OFFERED. The envelope's own question is whether a decaying restart peak beats a constant one on goal A, and it has never been measured in this tree. Two arms, 48,000 optimizer steps, OPT_LR_WAVELENGTH=6000 OPT_LR_WARMUP=1000 (8 fitted cycles), >= 3 seeds, everything else shipped: OPT_LR_DECAY=1.0 versus OPT_LR_DECAY=0.0. Read held-out bits/byte at the end and at the ~6000-step turn. FALSIFIER: if 0.0 wins by more than the seed spread, the default should move and this recommendation is wrong; if 1.0 wins or they tie, the default stands and the detector repair in finding 1 is the only change worth making. Run it AFTER stage 1 of finding 1's experiment, because if the multi-cycle arm loses to the single cycle outright then neither lever is on goal A's path.

Detector counts with damping live: same script, table rows 'wl=300 decay=0.0 ... shipped wraps=6 detected=2 final_amp=0.250000 mean_lr=4.7904e-04 (24.0% of peak)' against 'wl=300 decay=1.0 ... shipped ... mean_lr=4.0585e-04 (20.3% of peak)'.

CALL 2 -- st.grad_norms GROWS WITHOUT BOUND. RECOMMENDATION: REPLACE THE LIST WITH A FIXED LOG-SPACED HISTOGRAM CARRIED PER RUN SEGMENT, and say the resolution out loud in the report. The file-size argument is the weakest reason to act; the strong one is that the pooled whole-run p50/p99 cannot answer the question docs/04_CONTRACT.md's own Q-OPT-3 says it exists to answer.

THE COST, MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED. One float costs EXACTLY 9.00 bytes in the payload at every size tested (torch.save of {'grad_norms': list}, 1,000 / 6,000 / 48,000 / 200,000 elements -> 10,285 / 55,277 / 433,389 / 1,801,645 bytes). So: 48,000 optimizer steps (the run length src/opt/api.py::<module> is about) = 433 kB inside EVERY checkpoint; 280,000 steps (longrun.sh's own LR_STEPS=280000) = 2.52 MB. Resident, a 48,000-element python list of floats is ~1.54 MB (sizeof(list) plus 24 B per float object). The 'quadratic in the number of saves' phrase in src/opt/api.py::state_dict is, numerically: at longrun.sh's CKPT_EVERY=20000 over 280,000 steps at batch_windows=1 that is 14 saves and 9 * 20000 * (1+...+14) = 18.9 MB of grad-norm bytes written across the run. For scale, the base LM at the shipped LM_WIDTH=128 / LM_VOCAB_SLOTS=4096 is order 1.2M parameters, i.e. order 15 MB of fp32 weights plus AdamW moments -- so at 48k steps the list is a few percent of the file and at 280k it is a material fraction. NOT AN EMERGENCY. If file size were the only issue, 'do nothing' would be the right answer.

THE REAL COST IS THE ESTIMATOR, AND IT IS THE CONTRACT'S OWN COMPLAINT. docs/04_CONTRACT.md's Q-OPT-3 states the settling experiment as: 'Run the shipped configuration at OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0 and read opt.grad_norm.p50 and opt.grad_norm.p99 from OPT.counters across the whole run, INCLUDING THE WINDOW where held-out bits/byte turns from ~2.4 upward near step 6000. If p99 stays within a small multiple of p50 across that turn, clipping cannot be the mechanism.' That is a TIME-LOCALISED reading, and src/opt/api.py::counters renders exactly two pooled numbers over the whole run. Measured on a synthetic 48,000-step trace shaped like the one Q-OPT-3 describes (lognormal, drifting down, wider early, 0.2% spikes): the pooled p99 is 8.53 while the per-segment p99 runs 18.84 -> 13.34 -> 5.31 -> 4.22 -> 4.22 -> 3.35 -> 2.99 -> 2.37 across the run -- a 7.9x swing the single number hides. KEEPING THE FULL LIST DOES NOT FIX THIS EITHER, because counters() never exposes the list; the run pays 433 kB per save for a sample nothing reads at the resolution the question needs.

THE CARRIERS, MEASURED AGAINST THE EXACT p50/p99 OVER THE SAME 48,000 SAMPLES (exact p50=1.0731, p99=8.5323).
  RESERVOIR SAMPLE (uniform over the run), 30 independent draws per size: k=256 -> p50 error mean 4.3% worst 10.4%, p99 error mean 27.5% WORST 53.9%. k=1024 -> p50 2.2%/5.8%, p99 15.5%/43.0%. k=4096 -> p50 1.3%/3.0%, p99 6.6%/19.4%. The tail is the number a clipping decision reads and the reservoir is worst exactly there. IT ALSO HAS A STRUCTURAL DISQUALIFIER: it needs a random stream, and OPT has none -- src/spine/compose.py::RNG_SUBSYSTEMS is ('lm','sig','fabric','memory', 'domains','world','tok.dropout','data.synth','data.holdout','eval') with no 'opt'. Minting one is an edit to compose.py, a new name in the isolation sweep's per-package fingerprints, and a fifth entry in the RNG family the standing brief says has bitten four times. Loses twice.
  FIXED RING BUFFER (last k): k=1024 -> p50 -42.2%, p99 -73.3%. k=4096 -> -39.9% / -70.6%. k=12000 -> -33.9% / -68.2%. This is not an approximation, it is a different measurement, and it is the exact defect src/opt/api.py::state_dict already names in the other direction ('a norm distribution that restarts empty makes opt.grad_norm.p50/p99 describe the tail of a run rather than the run'). Loses outright.
  STREAMING QUANTILE SKETCH (t-digest / Greenwald-Khanna): the best tail fidelity per byte of the four, and it loses on defensibility rather than on quality. It is 150-300 lines of numerics this project would own, its guarantee is a probabilistic bound on RANK which is awkward to print in a report a reader has to trust, and numpy is not importable in this environment (torch prints 'Failed to initialize NumPy: No module named numpy' on every import), so it would be pure-python and hot on a per-step path. Reconsider only if the histogram's resolution proves too coarse.
  LOG-SPACED HISTOGRAM, bins over 1e-6..1e4 with an underflow and an overflow bin: 100 bins -> p50 +4.56%, p99 +4.46% (102 ints). 200 bins -> -1.29% / -1.39% (202 ints). 400 bins -> +1.59% / +1.49%. 1000 bins -> +1.01% / +0.91%. The RANK is exact; only the VALUE is quantised, to a known factor per bin (x1.1220 at 200 bins). WINS ON FOUR PROPERTIES THE OTHERS LACK: bounded memory independent of run length; DETERMINISTIC, so tests/test_determinism's fingerprints do not move and no RNG stream is minted; counts COMPOSE ACROSS A RESUME BY ADDITION, which is what src/opt/api.py::state_dict's paragraph actually requires; and the error is STATEABLE as one number in the report rather than as a confidence interval.

THE SHAPE I RECOMMEND. 24 run segments x 200 bins = 4,848 integers, ~44 kB in the payload, CONSTANT in run length (against 433 kB and rising today, 2.52 MB at 280k steps). counters() keeps opt.grad_norm.p50 / p99 as the pooled pair -- computed by summing the segment histograms, so the name still means the whole run -- and GAINS opt.grad_norm.resolution (the per-bin factor) plus a per-segment p50/p99 series, which is the thing Q-OPT-3 asks for. THE NAMING IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART: because the value is bin-quantised, the report must say so, or this becomes the project's characteristic failure -- an instrument reporting something other than what it names. The gate reason is the natural place ('read in maybe_step between the gradient's last use and the zero_grad; rendered here, never computed here' gains 'quantised to a factor of 1.1220 per bin over 1e-6..1e4').

THE 'DO NOTHING YET' CASE, STATED HONESTLY. It is defensible. At 48,000 steps the cost is 433 kB in a file already holding order 15 MB of optimizer state, the exact whole-run p50/p99 are the most defensible estimators available, and nothing in the tree currently READS the norms at higher resolution because src/eval/api.py::curve_probe is deferred and the turn cannot be located in a report yet. If the owner is not going to run Q-OPT-3's experiment, do nothing and revisit when 280k-step runs become routine.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT -- IT IS Q-OPT-3'S OWN, AND IT IS GPU WORK. Shipped configuration, OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0, 48,000 optimizer steps, >= 3 seeds; dump the gradient-norm distribution PER SEGMENT alongside held-out bits/byte. FALSIFIER: if p99/p50 is flat across the ~6000-step turn, clipping is not the mechanism, OPT_GRAD_CLIP retires to docs/dropped_levers.md with the number attached, and the carrier question shrinks to a file-size question where 'do nothing' wins. If p99/p50 spikes at or before the turn, the matched OPT_GRAD_CLIP=0 vs 1.0 pair is the next run, and the time-resolved carrier has to exist BEFORE it, because the pooled pair cannot show where the spike sits.
findings.repro: Serialised cost: .../own/gn_cost.py -> torch.save({'grad_norms': list}) at n = 1000/6000/48000/200000 gives 10285/55277/433389/1801645 bytes, 9.00 B per float at every size; the same data as a float32 tensor is 193,577 B and as float16 97,577 B. Carrier comparison: .../own/gn_carriers.py -> sections A (reservoir, 30 trials per k), B (ring buffer), C (log histogram, 100/200/400/1000 bins), D (24-segment histogram, p99 per segment). RNG absence: grep -n 'rng|random' src/opt/api.py src/opt/levers.py returns nothing; src/spine/compose.py::RNG_SUBSYSTEMS lists ten names, none of them OPT. numpy absence: any torch import in this environment prints 'Failed to initialize NumPy: No module named numpy'.

findings.detail:
CALL 3 -- DOES WarmupReport NEED A FOURTH VERDICT? YES, AND THE CUT THE QUESTION PROPOSES IS THE WRONG ONE. The brief asks whether 'the arms where NO step ran' deserve their own verdict. Measured, that is not where the damage is: there are arms that RUN THE WHOLE BUDGET, take probes, and still cannot produce any verdict at all -- and one of them reports 'budget' on a fully collapsed encoder. The predicate that separates the states is not 'did a step run' but 'could any verdict have been produced', and src/sig/api.py::warm_up already computes it, as `collapse_points`.

WHAT EACH VERDICT MEANS TODAY (src/sig/api.py::warm_up docstring, after the SIG repair): 'plateau' = separation flat within warmup_plateau_eps and >= 0.85 of its own peak; 'collapsing' = separation below 0.7 of its peak or below 0.15 absolute -- 'a RUN-LEVEL FAILURE'; 'budget' = 'no stop fired -- INCLUDING THE ARMS WHERE NO STEP RAN AT ALL, and the record cannot tell those apart, so read it beside the two counters that can.'

THE ARMS THAT PRODUCE 'budget', ENUMERATED AND DRIVEN LIVE (learned encoder unless stated, width_units=64, 20,000-unit stream):
  B1 SIG_MODE=bigram              -> steps=0   probes=0  sep_final=None      gate UNREACHABLE
  B2 SIG_WARMUP=0                 -> steps=0   probes=0  sep_final=None      gate UNREACHABLE
  B3 probe_every(400) > budget(300)-> steps=300 probes=0  sep_final=None      gate UNREACHABLE
  B4 800/300 with MIN_FRAC=0.9    -> steps=800 probes=2  sep_final=0.981      gate UNREACHABLE
  B5 400/100 with EPS=0.0         -> steps=400 probes=4  sep_final=0.989      gate armed-but-0
B1 and B2 are structurally inert and the counters DO separate them (steps==0), exactly as the docstring claims. B3 and B4 are NOT covered by that claim: both ran the entire budget, B4 took two probes, and neither could reach a verdict -- in B3 because no probe exists, in B4 because no probe lands at or after the floor. B5 is the only arm where 'budget' means what the docstring wants it to mean: the condition was measured and not met.

SO YES, TWO STATES ARE CONFLATED, AND THE CONFLATION IS EXACTLY spine/gate.py::Gate'S OWN THREE STATES APPLIED TO A RECORD INSTEAD OF A GATE. 'budget' currently spans UNREACHABLE (B1-B4: no verdict could be produced) and ARMED-BUT-0 (B5: a verdict could be produced and none was). The tree already has the vocabulary and the discipline; the record does not carry it.

AND IT CAN MISLEAD THE COMPOSITION ROOT, WHICH THE DOCSTRING SAYS MUST ACT ON THIS. Driving B4 WITH A COLLAPSED ENCODER (every window identical): verdict='budget', probes=2, separation_final=5.96e-08. src/spine/compose.py branches on `if sysm.warmup is not None and sysm.warmup.verdict == 'collapsing'`, so the RUN-LEVEL FAILURE warning -- the one that says 'Every window of this run is routed through that encoder, so SHIFT_DIST, the boundary count and the domain count downstream of it are measurements of a collapsed space' -- IS NOT EMITTED on a run whose encoder is fully collapsed. Driving B3 with the same stream: verdict='budget', separation_final=None, so no surface anywhere in the tree carries the truth. This is the historical failure the module exists to remove (0.16 -> 0.05 read as a converged plateau, 0 boundaries, 1 domain, every downstream line still printed), restored one level up, and reachable from legal lever values -- SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC=0.9 is inside the declared unit interval.

RECOMMENDATION. A fourth spelling on WarmupReport.verdict and on the sig.warmup_verdict counter, returned exactly when no verdict could have been produced: `mode != 'learned' or budget < 1 or not collapse_points`. I would spell it 'unmeasured' rather than 'unreachable' so that it reads as a statement about the RUN and leaves 'unreachable' to Gate, where it is a statement about a mechanism. steps and probes keep their present values, so B1/B2 (steps==0) stay distinguishable from B3/B4 (steps>0) off the counters. 'budget' then means, unambiguously, 'the budget was spent, the stop condition was evaluated, and it was not met' -- which is what a reader already assumes it means.

ALTERNATIVES.
  (a) DO NOTHING -- what the SIG repair agent chose, correcting the DEFINITION in the docstring rather than the record. Costs nothing today and is honest prose, but it leaves the composition root's single branch reading a value that is false on B4, and prose does not reach a branch.
  (b) MAKE THE ROOT READ separation_final INSTEAD OF verdict. Rejected: the 0.15 threshold would then live in src/spine/compose.py as well as in src/sig/api.py::_stop_verdict -- one number in two places, which is the L1 shape src/sig/levers.py::SIGLevers already records against this very lever family, and the root would be re-deciding a question SIG owns.
  (c) MAKE warm_up REFUSE when collapse_points is empty. Rejected: it takes a policy this tree has deliberately not taken -- src/spine/compose.py says in writing 'the root does not refuse the run here, because neither sig/api.py::warm_up nor the contract says what acting on this verdict is' and 'an unruled one taken silently at a call site is how a policy gets into this tree without anybody choosing it'. It would also abort SIG_MODE=bigram, a legitimate control arm.
  (d) LEAVE IT TO THE GATE. The Gate ALREADY separates B4 from B5 (measured: B4 UNREACHABLE, B5 armed-but-0), so for a HUMAN reading the report the information exists. It loses because WarmupReport is what the docstring says the root must act on, and the root reads sysm.warmup.verdict, not st.gates. The Gate is the right instrument for a reader and the wrong one for a branch.

WHAT IT COSTS. A record-type change touching three files outside SIG's two: docs/04_CONTRACT.md's SIG section, src/spine/compose.py's warmup ASSEMBLY_ORDER row prose, and the root's branch (which should become `verdict in ('collapsing',)` unchanged plus a second, quieter warning on 'unmeasured' -- an unmeasured encoder is not a failure, but it is not a clean bill of health either). No lever, no wire, no RNG stream, no signature change. It forecloses nothing: a fifth spelling could still be added later if the plateau arm ever needs its own inert state.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Run the shipped SIG configuration on the REAL corpus with SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY lowered to 100 so the curve has eight points, >= 3 seeds, and read the separation curve and sig.warmup_verdict. FALSIFIER: if the real corpus's separation curve never approaches 0.15 and never falls to 0.7 of its peak, then 'collapsing' is not reachable in practice on real data, the B3/B4 conflation is bookkeeping, and alternative (a) is the right answer. If it DOES approach either bound -- and the project's own historical record is a 0.16 -> 0.05 collapse on a single-corpus stream -- then the conflation is live on the encoder every routing decision in the run goes through, and the fourth verdict should land before the next long run. This costs minutes of GPU, not hours, and it is the cheapest experiment in this report.

Output lines B1..B5 as tabulated, plus 'B4 with a COLLAPSED encoder' -> {verdict: budget, steps: 800, probes: 2, sep_final: 5.960464477539063e-08, gate: UNREACHABLE} and 'B3 with a COLLAPSED encoder' -> {verdict: budget, steps: 300, probes: 0, sep_final: null}. THAT IS NO LONGER TRUE IN THE CURRENT TREE. src/spine/compose.py::compose now binds `sysm.warmup = sig_api.warm_up(...)` and, on verdict=='collapsing', appends a 'RUN-LEVEL FAILURE, not a warning' entry to sysm.warnings naming separation_final, separation_peak, steps and probes, with an explicit comment that the entry 'IS A CARRIER AND NOT A POLICY'. I re-verified this before writing finding 7 so that the fourth-verdict recommendation is made against the root that exists rather than the one the SIG repair agent saw. THE RESIDUE THAT REMAINS is not the binding but the branch: it reads only 'collapsing', which is exactly why the B3/B4 conflation in finding 7 can reach it.

findings.detail:
CALL 4 -- SHOULD THE SHIPPED SIG_WARMUP DEFAULTS CHANGE? RECOMMENDATION: MOVE SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY FROM 500 TO 100, AND LEAVE SIG_WARMUP AT 800 FOR NOW. One lever, and it is the instrument lever rather than the training lever.

HOW MANY PROBES THE SHIPPED DEFAULTS ADMIT: EXACTLY ONE, AND ZERO OF THEM CAN STOP ANYTHING. src/sig/api.py::warm_up builds `grid = tuple(range(probe_every, budget + 1, probe_every))`, `stop_points = tuple(t for i, t in enumerate(grid) if i >= 1 and t >= floor)` and `collapse_points = tuple(t for t in grid if t >= floor)`, with `floor = int(warmup_min_frac * budget)`. At the shipped 800 / 500 / 0.25: floor=200, grid=(500,), stop_points=(), collapse_points=(500,). Driven live on a separable stream: probes=1, steps=800, verdict='budget', Gate sig.adaptive_stop UNREACHABLE. The adaptive stop -- which the old file calls its '#1 startup cost saving' -- is off in every default run, and the curve the whole mechanism reads has ONE POINT, which cannot distinguish 'separated and stable' from 'separated and about to fall'.

WHAT THE DETECTOR NEEDS, MEASURED ACROSS THE GRID (SIG_WARMUP=800, MIN_FRAC=0.25, floor=200):
  probe_every=500 -> 1 probe,  0 stop points
  probe_every=400 -> 2 probes, 1 stop point  at step 800 (the LAST step: the verdict becomes producible but no budget is saved)
  probe_every=300 -> 2 probes, 1 stop point  at 600
  probe_every=250 -> 3 probes, 2 stop points at 500, 750
  probe_every=200 -> 4 probes, 3 stop points at 400, 600, 800
  probe_every=100 -> 8 probes, 7 stop points from 200
  probe_every= 50 -> 16 probes, 13 stop points from 200
src/sig/levers.py::SIGLevers.warmup_probe_every says 'Lowering this lever to 200 or below is what buys back the plateau stop'. Measured, that is right about the SAVING and one notch conservative about the VERDICT: 400 and 300 make the plateau verdict producible, they just cannot save anything worth having.

WHAT PROBING MORE COSTS: ESSENTIALLY NOTHING, AND THIS IS THE DECIDING NUMBER. Timed on CPU fp32 at the shipped SIG_CONTRASTIVE_BATCH=48 and width_units=64: one warm-up optimizer step 3.54 ms, one separation probe 0.57 ms -- probe/step = 0.16x. Total probe overhead as a share of a full 800-step budget: 0.02% at probe_every=500, 0.04% at 400, 0.08% at 200, 0.16% at 100, 0.32% at 50. A default that cannot exercise its own failure detector is being paid for with two hundredths of one percent of the budget.

IT IS THE ISSUES P1-C11 DISEASE, IN A CLOCK KIND THE P1-C11 DETECTOR CANNOT SEE. docs/04_CONTRACT.md records 'cadence_audit was a row nobody called ... the one statement that makes ISSUES P1-C11 visible -- ten cadence defaults longer than a 937-window run -- never ran'. That audit now runs, but src/spine/compose.py::compose passes it a FIVE-KEY mapping of units.Windows periods (curve, dom.manage, fab.manage, dom.rekey, ckpt) and src/spine/derive.py::cadences_that_cannot_fire refuses anything that is not units.Windows. SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY is units.Steps and pre-loop, so no audit in this tree can ever report it. The one thing that DOES report it is the gate reason src/sig/api.py::warm_up prints, and it prints UNREACHABLE on every default run.

WHY 100 AND NOT SOMETHING ELSE. (i) It divides 800 exactly, so the last probe lands on the last step and no part of the budget is spent unmeasured. (ii) 8 probes give the curve enough resolution that 'still climbing' and 'flat' are distinguishable, which one point and two points are not. (iii) 7 of the 8 are stop-eligible, so the saving is real rather than nominal. (iv) 0.16% of the budget. (v) It leaves SIG_WARMUP untouched, so the recorded hazard in src/sig/levers.py::SIGLevers.warmup -- '1-NN corpus accuracy PEAKS at roughly 1000-4000 steps and DEGRADES after' and 'two runs changed the threshold rule AND ENC_WARMUP together, so neither result can be attributed to either change' -- is not disturbed.

⚠ SAY THIS OUT LOUD: IT IS A TRAINING CHANGE, NOT A REPORTING ONE. With the plateau stop live, a run may spend FEWER than 800 encoder steps, and the encoder is what every window in the run is routed through. Measured on a synthetic separable stream, 800/100 stopped at step 200 with verdict='plateau' and 800/200 stopped at step 400, against 800 steps at the shipped cadence -- a 75% and 50% reduction in warm-up. On a random-byte stream the separation saturates almost immediately so those stop points are optimistic, but the direction is right and the owner should not be told this is free.

ALTERNATIVES.
  (a) 200 instead of 100: 4 probes, 3 stop-eligible, 0.08% overhead. Endorsed by the levers file's own sentence. Loses to 100 only on curve resolution and by 0.08% of the budget. A perfectly good second choice if the owner wants the smallest move that works.
  (b) RAISE SIG_WARMUP TO 2000-4000 AND LEAVE THE CADENCE AT 500 (4 or 8 probes, 3 or 7 stop-eligible). This also makes the stop live, and it has an independent argument -- the recorded 1-NN peak is at 1000-4000 steps and the shipped budget of 800 is BELOW that band. It loses HERE because it entangles an instrument repair with a change to what the encoder is, and because SIG_WARMUP=800 is the setting every archived SIG result was taken at. It is the right SECOND experiment, once the cadence can see the curve.
  (c) CHANGE BOTH AT ONCE. Rejected on the file's own carry-forward hazard: 'two runs changed the threshold rule AND ENC_WARMUP together, so neither result can be attributed to either change'. Repeating that would be the same mistake with the same lever.
  (d) DO NOTHING AND RELY ON THE COLLAPSE ALARM. Defensible after the SIG repair: the RUN-LEVEL FAILURE verdict IS now reachable at 800/500 (driven live on a degenerate stream: verdict='collapsing' at step 500, probes=1). It loses because a one-point curve gives the collapse arm only its ABSOLUTE test (sep < 0.15); the RELATIVE arm (sep < 0.7 * peak) is vacuous on one point by src/sig/api.py::_stop_verdict's own reasoning, so an encoder that separates well and then halves is invisible -- and 0.16 -> 0.05 is precisely the historical failure.
  (e) MAKE THE CADENCE A FRACTION OF THE BUDGET, as SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC already is. Attractive, because it makes the one-probe pairing unrepresentable by construction rather than reported. Rejected for now: it changes a lever's UNIT (units.Steps -> FRACTION), which is a census-visible change and a second thing to argue about, and src/sig/levers.py::SIGLevers.warmup_min_frac already records that expressing a floor as a fraction did NOT make the bad pairing impossible, only out-of-range. Worth revisiting if the cadence default has to be argued a second time.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT -- REAL CORPUS, AND IT IS CHEAP GPU. A 2x3 grid: SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY in {500, 100} x SIG_WARMUP in {800, 2000, 4000}, >= 3 seeds, everything else shipped. Record (1) the separation curve, (2) where the plateau stop fires if it does, (3) the downstream DOM boundary count and domain count, (4) final held-out bits/byte. FALSIFIER FOR THE CADENCE CHANGE: if at 800/100 the plateau stop fires early AND the boundary count, domain count and final bits/byte are all within the seed spread of 800/500, the cadence change is free and should be taken. If the early stop MOVES the domain count, then the stop is buying a DIFFERENT ENCODER and the real ruling is about SIG_WARMUP_MIN_FRAC, not about the cadence -- and the cadence should still move, but the floor should rise with it. FALSIFIER FOR THE BUDGET: if the 4000-step curve is still climbing at step 800, SIG_WARMUP=800 is below the knee on real data and the budget is the thing to change; if it is flat by 800, 800 stands and alternative (b) is dead.

Timings: .../own/sig_cost.py -> 50 timed _draw_pairs+_contrastive_loss+step iterations (3.54 ms/step) against 50 timed _separation calls (0.57 ms/probe). Periods mapping: grep -n 'periods = ' src/spine/compose.py -> five keys, all units.Windows accessors.

findings.detail:
A SECOND GATE FOR THE COLLAPSE STOP -- reporting-only, raised by me while measuring Call 4, and cheap. MEASURED: at the shipped SIG_WARMUP=800 / SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=500 on a degenerate stream, warm_up STOPS EARLY at step 500 with verdict='collapsing', and the only gate in the package about stopping prints 'Gate sig.adaptive_stop: UNREACHABLE (200 vs 800) -- SIG_WARMUP_PROBE_EVERY=500 against SIG_WARMUP=800 puts 1 separation probe(s) in the budget ... so the flatness test ... has nothing to compare.' The reason sentence is honest and even names the collapse arm as still live, but UNREACHABLE is the state word a reader scans for, and it is the wrong word for a run on which a stop fired. This is the tree's own standard applied to itself: 'armed, did not fire' printed for a mechanism that CANNOT fire is a defect, and the mirror -- 'unreachable' printed on a run that stopped -- is the same class.

RECOMMENDATION: a second Gate, sig.collapse_stop, whose reachability grid is `collapse_points` (already computed in warm_up), whose fired is `verdict == 'collapsing'`, and whose arithmetic is (floor, budget, the collapse probe steps). It changes no training, needs no lever, no wire and no RNG stream, and it costs one line in the SIG ledger plus one DID IT FIRE name in warm_up's docstring.

ALTERNATIVES. (a) Widen sig.adaptive_stop to mean 'any early stop': loses because its value (floor vs budget) names arithmetic only the plateau arm uses, and src/sig/api.py::_stop_verdict's docstring is explicit that 'THE TWO ARMS NEED DIFFERENT AMOUNTS OF CURVE AND THIS FUNCTION IS WHERE THAT IS DECIDED' -- merging them in the report undoes in the ledger what the repair just did in the code. (b) Leave it: defensible, because the reason string does carry the information and sig.warmup_verdict carries the outcome; it loses on the one thing this project measures itself by, which is whether a reader who did not write the code draws the right conclusion. (c) Take the Call 4 cadence change and the problem mostly disappears (at 100 the gate is reachable, so the UNREACHABLE-with-a-stop combination stops occurring): TRUE, and it is the reason this is severity low rather than medium -- but the combination remains reachable at any cadence a user sets, so the gate is still worth having.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT is not a GPU run, it is a reader test, and I will name it rather than pretend otherwise: show the shipped report for the 800/500 collapsed-stream run to someone who did not write SIG and ask what the warm-up did. If they read 'UNREACHABLE' and conclude no stop occurred, the gate is needed. If they read the reason sentence and get it right, leave it.
